summary: Deep editorial audit of 14 pages (homepage incl. rendered HTML, 5 hubs, 8 flagships) with quality/search-readiness scores and top-3 fixes each; plus 5 writer-ready rewrite briefs for the weakest pages: gas-customer-charge-explained, 24-delivery-charge-vs-supply-charge, duct-leaks-symptoms, drought-surcharge-on-water-bill, why-is-my-furnace-blowing-cold-air.
findings: PER-PAGE SCORES AND TOP-3 FIXES. (1) Homepage (content/_index.md + public/index.html): quality 9/10, search-readiness 8/10. Rendered UX strong: single H1 'Understand Every Line on Your Utility Bill', lede 'We translate electricity, gas, and water bills into decisions you can actually make', dual CTA, 'Searchers want:' quick-links strip, guided cards, Most Read, newsletter, trust strip (editorial-policy/team/methodology/affiliate-disclosure), footer Amazon disclosure, good a11y (skip-link, aria labels). Fixes: bare title tag 'Utility Explained' wastes SERP space; guide-count register shows 84 via layouts/_default/index.html lines 21-22 while repo holds 89 files (85 published after 4 drafts) — count drift and aria-label duplicates visible text; no ItemList/person E-E-A-T signal in hero. (2) electricity-explained hub: 8/10, 7/10 — best hub, has figure with descriptive alt and worked bill math, but no Quick Answer block; duplicate links to same slugs with different anchors (01-how-to-read-your-electric-bill and 24-delivery-charge-vs-supply each appear twice, 03-why-is-my-electric-bill-so-high three times); no byline. (3) gas-explained hub: 8/10, 7/10 — good therm math (1 therm = 29.3 kWh), FAQ, deep-linked related guides; same three fixes; supply example $1.50/therm unanchored vs $1.91 EIA May 2026 cited elsewhere. (4) water-explained hub: 8/10, 7/10 — excellent unit chain (1 CCF = 748 gallons; 6 CCF = 4,488 gallons), winter-average sewer explanation; missing Quick Answer/byline, ccf-calculator not linked from units section; add one worked combined monthly total. (5) heating-cooling-explained hub: 8/10, 7/10 — densest topic hub; same gaps; repair-vs-replace needs a numeric decision table; should cross-link duct-leaks post. (6) utility-bills-costs-explained hub: 9/10, 8/10 — the model hub: Quick AnswerH2, component tables, rate structures, budgeting, faq-schema confirmed; add byline; this hub should funnel to complete-guide-understanding-utility-bill explicitly.

PER-PAGE SCORES CONTINUED. (7) complete-guide-understanding-utility-bill: 7.5/10, 7.5/10 — clean procedural workflow (5 steps, charge-mapping table of internal links, DOE sources) but the LEANEST flagship at 9,024 bytes with zero visuals, no FAQ/faq-schema, no worked dollar example; title was renamed to 'A Practical Workflow for Understanding Your Utility Bill' while slug + keywords still target the 'complete guide/understand utility bill' head term — mismatch, underperforming its potential as the site's canonical hub-spoke for all bill-reading queries; it also consumes alias /blog/how-to-read-your-utility-bill/. (8) 2026-utility-cost-index-by-state: DRAFT ONLY (draft: true) — 50-state table with honest usage-standardization notes, but its national figure $262/month contradicts the live alias target's $375/month narrow basket; recommend remove-or-redirect (archive outside content/). (9) average-utility-bills-by-state-2026 (the consolidation target): 8.5/10, 8.5/10 — best Quick Answer on site (narrow vs broad basket defined), jump-row, honest 17-state sample, faq-schema; fixes: mixed raw-HTML formatting hygiene, Hawaii FAQ number $453 vs body $324 reconciliation needed, 'How we calculate' should sit above the first table. (10) how-to-lower-electric-bill-complete-guide: 9/10, 9/10 — model page: dated EIA/DOE sources, About-our-numbers block, cost-tiered Quick Answer with Start-here sequencing, product boxes matched to steps per the affiliate plan; only nits: $144 (2024) vs $165 (18.34c x 900) reconciliation, confirm faq-schema. (11) 07-gas-bill-too-high: 9/10, 8.5/10 — ranked causes, HDD worked example, contextual Nest placement, faq-schema; fixes: duplicate front-matter source entries (energy.gov and energystar.gov each listed twice), 65F/55F 'maximum savings' line needs clarity labeling. (12) 30-sudden-spike: 8.5/10, 8/10 — 5-cause Quick Answer + 12 steps + flowchart; fixes: has FAQ heading but NO faq-schema shortcode (grep confirms absence), steps 11-12 duplicate the dispute page (compress to summary + handoff link), 12-step length wants a jump-row. (13) how-to-dispute-utility-bill: 9/10, 8.5/10 — YMYL-correct (keep paying undisputed portion, Texas protection cited), sample letter, evidence log, PUC escalation; fixes: no FAQ/faq-schema on the most question-shaped topic; letter needs a copy/print affordance; state-variance callout. (14) moving-utilities-checklist: 7.5/10, 7.5/10 — strong Quick Answer (turn-off day after / turn-on day before), week-by-week table, faq-schema; CRITICAL: live page still ships an '## Image Prompts' authoring-scaffolding section (3 numbered generation prompts) in rendered output — must be deleted; sources thin (bare dominionenergy.com); the good visuals its prompts describe were never built.

FLAGSHIP VERDICT (mission question): yes, one flagship is actively underperforming — complete-guide-understanding-utility-bill. Evidence: smallest flagship (9024 vs 17-29KB siblings), no visuals, no FAQ, no worked example, title/slug mismatch after rename, yet it holds the homepage 'Essential guides' slot and the alias for the how-to-read-your-utility-bill URL. It is positioned as the consolidation epicenter but lacks the concrete worked example that would justify its rank. Secondary underperformer: 2026-utility-cost-index-by-state exists only as an unpublished draft whose $262 QA contradicts the live $375 page — publication would create a site-wide number conflict.

WEAK-PAGE DIAGNOSIS (basis for all 5 briefs): the shortlisted pages (updated 2026-08-23 as a batch) share a de-hallucination-overcorrection pattern: every sentence hedges ('whose definitions... depend on the serving utility and tariff'), zero verified dollar figures, zero named utilities, zero worked math. Proof: why-is-my-furnace-blowing-cold-air greps 0 hits for dollar amounts or degree numbers, 485 words; gas-customer-charge and 24-delivery-vs-supply have no $ figures; meanwhile 17-what-is-customer-charge (11,430 bytes, updated 2026-08-29) demonstrates the house standard with a 'Verified customer charges (published rates, not ranges)' table. The 08-23 batch predates the SQ-064 08-29 deepening waves, so briefs are not duplicating done work.

DRAFT CLUSTER (SEO risk, action vocabulary used): 4 files carry draft: true — 2026-utility-cost-index-by-state, gas-customer-charge-explained, how-to-read-your-utility-bill, supply-vs-delivery-charges-electricity. Two live flagships alias-consume two of these URLs (average-utility-bills aliases 2026-utility-cost-index; complete-guide aliases how-to-read-your-utility-bill; rendered public/blog/how-to-read-your-utility-bill/index.html canonicals to complete-guide with a refresh meta). Recommend: delete/archive the two consumed drafts (remove-or-redirect), and decide publish-or-delete for the other two; highest urgency is the 2026-index draft because publishing it would reintroduce the contradictory $262 figure.

E-E-A-T BACKBONE: 5 author pages exist; margaret-harrington.md honestly discloses desk-byline status and AI assistance ('Guides may use AI assistance during drafting'). Flagships carry author + updated dates; hubs carry neither author nor visible updated stamp in body. Trust pages are linked sitewide from footer + trust strip. Gap: hub template should add a compact byline/updated line matching flagship layout.

MONETIZATION FIT: affiliate placements observed only on content-appropriate pages (Kill A Watt/Nest inside savings and thermostat causes), none on crisis or fee pages, consistent with AFFILIATE-PLACEMENTS-2026-08-28 doctrine; keep rewrites product-free until substantive content exists.

SUBSTITUTION NOTE: net-metering-explained and which-rate-plan-is-right-for-me were read and are NOT weak enough to brief (decision tables, market-context questions, cross-links present); how-to-read-your-utility-bill could not be briefed because it is a draft consumed as an alias by complete-guide; net-metering (zero dollar figures) would be brief #6 if capacity opens.
